newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia ends Aeroflot Moscow-Riga ban.
newsitem.headline: Latvia ends Aeroflot Moscow-Riga ban.

text.p: Latvia has given Russian airline Aeroflot permission to resume flights between Moscow and Riga and hopes to be allowed to start a service between the two capitals itself, a transport official said on Wednesday.
Arnis Muizhnieks, the head of the Latvian transport ministry's aviation department, said that Aeroflot can resume its service at any time.

He also said that Latvian Transport Minister Vilis Krishtopans, who is to visit Moscow in December, would hold talks on allowing Latvia's Air Baltic, in which Scandinavian Airlines has a large stake, to fly to Russia.
"We think that we can solve the problems with outstanding debt," Muizhnieks told Reuters.
Russia has refused to allow Air Baltic to fly to Moscow as the previous state-owned Latvian airline Latavio owed some $2.8 million for airport services.
The Aeroflot flights were suspended as Latvia said Russia's refusal over Air Baltic meant there was no flight parity between the two countries.
Muizhnieks said Latvia was ready to pay the debt, meaning that any financial obstacles over allowing Air Baltic to fly to Russia would be removed.
